claims.text: Ab initio calculations can accurately predict how local chemical order and short-range order affect the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
Machine-learning models can accurately predict how local chemical order and short-range order affect the mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
Computational models can accurately predict the mechanical effects of dynamically developing interstitial-driven local chemical order.
Short-range order is present in medium- and high-entropy alloys and changes with heat treatment.
Dynamic interstitial-driven local chemical order can contribute to high yield strength and work hardening in FCC high-entropy alloys.
The proposed computational predictions will enable the design of new high-entropy-alloy compositions.
The proposed computational predictions will enable the design of new high-entropy-alloy microstructures.
Alloys designed by the proposed methods will have greater strength than alloys designed using current strategies.
Alloys designed by the proposed methods will have greater ductility than alloys designed using current strategies.
Alloys designed by the proposed methods will have improved Young's modulus relative to alloys designed using current strategies.
Alloys designed by the proposed methods will have improved fracture resistance relative to alloys designed using current strategies.
The proposed methodology applies under operating conditions relevant to structural applications.
Current methods for designing high-entropy alloys are limited in their treatment of local and short-range order.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvement achievable with the proposed methods is uncertain.
A comparison against alloys designed using current methods can falsify the hypothesis if no improved combination of the four target properties is observed.
